open_decisions.question: S-06-002 is authorised (HD-S06-002-AUTHORISE resolved). Per the owner's condition, the expansion-vs-contraction predicate was pinned from the authoritative repository. The CONCEPT is uniquely defined (contraction = non-broadening within the verified boundary, auto-activated by Admin/Marketing; expansion = same-host broadening, OrganizationAdmin dual control; new host is never an expansion; PRULE-021 is the admission predicate). But the classification PREDICATE is NOT pinned to an implementable level: (1) no classifier fixtures exist (MTX-029 tests assume a change is already labelled and test only routing/authority); (2) no algorithm is given for the broadening/subset test over include/exclude path-prefix sets; (3) it is unresolved whether a query_handling change (which does not change the PRULE-021 allow set but changes canonical-URL multiplicity) counts as broadening. Point 3 has two materially different valid readings with opposite dual-control outcomes, and misclassification is a scope-boundary security risk. How should the contraction-vs-expansion classifier be defined?
open_decisions.recommended_option: Option A: ratify 'broadening = the PRULE-021 admitted (allow) set grows'; classify a proposed policy as a CONTRACTION iff its admitted URL set is a subset of the current active policy's admitted set (PRULE-021 as the oracle), else an EXPANSION (fail-closed: any non-strict-subset change is an expansion); rule query_handling broadening-NEUTRAL (a query-only change is a contraction). Host/scheme/port beyond the verified boundary is a boundary violation, not a classification.
options: A (recommended): broadening = the PRULE-021 allow set grows; contraction iff proposed admitted-set is a subset of current (fail-closed to expansion otherwise); query_handling broadening-neutral
B: broadening includes query-handling widening (allowlist -> retain_all, which increases distinct crawl targets) as an expansion requiring dual control
C: a different classifier the owner specifies (e.g. a purely syntactic include/exclude comparison), or an owner-provided fixture set to pin the boundary
